chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'We do not know what to do with the people. If we narrate to them what we heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), they laugh, and if we remain silent, it is not bearable for us.'

He said, so Zamrah ibn Ma'bad said, 'Narrate to us.' So he said: 'Do you know what the enemy of Allah says when he is carried on his bier?' So we said, 'No.' He said: 'For he says to his bearers: Do you not hear that I am complaining to you? The enemy of Allah deceived me and imprisoned me, then did not release me. And I complain to you of brothers with whom I established brotherhood, so they abandoned me. And I complain to you of children whom I protected, so they abandoned me. And I complain to you of a house in which I spent my earnings, so its inhabitants became others than me. So be kind to me and do not hasten.'
He said, so Zamrah said, 'O Abu al-Hasan! If he speaks with this speech, he is likely to pounce upon the necks of those who carry him.'

He said, so Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah, if Zamrah has ridiculed the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then seize him with a seizure of grief/sorrow.'

He said, so he remained for forty days, then died, and a slave of his was present with him. He said, so when he was buried, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) came to him and sat by him, and said to him, 'From where have you come, O so-and-so?' He said, 'From the funeral of Zamrah. I placed my face upon him when the soil was leveled over him, and I heard his voice. By Allah, I recognized it just as I recognized it when he was alive.'

'He was saying: Woe to you, O Zamrah ibn Ma'bad! Today every friend has abandoned you, and your destination has become the Hellfire, wherein is your dwelling, your overnight stay, and your daytime stay.'

He said, so Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'I ask Allah for well-being. This is the recompense of the one who ridicules the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.سَرِيرِهِ: His bier/couch for carrying the dead
key_terms.ضَمْرَةُ بْنُ مَعْبَدٍ: Zamrah ibn Ma'bad, the companion who ridiculed hadith
key_terms.عَدُوُّ اللَّهِ: Enemy of Allah, a title often used for Zamrah in this context

ai.seo_question: What happened to Zamrah ibn Ma'bad after he ridiculed the hadith of the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of *al-tajassus* (spiritual inquiry) in the grave, where the deceased retains consciousness and communication with the living. Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) specifically links the ridicule of prophetic traditions to a loss of spiritual support, as Zamrah’s friends, family, and wealth—his worldly anchors—fail to aid him in the Hereafter. The narrative serves as a practical warning against dismissing religious knowledge, emphasizing that the grave is a place of reckoning where one’s relationship with the Ahl al-Bayt and the Prophet determines their fate.
